writing.focus: Summarising denser academic information with qualified comparisons
writing.prompt: This is original practice material, not an official test. The table below shows results from a freshwater microplastic sampling study on the River Alder in 2024 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Note the study limitations where they affect interpretation. Write at least 150 words in about 20 minutes. Table data: Site | Season | Samples taken | Mean particles per litre | Fibres as share of particles | Samples above 10 particles per litre. Upstream Rural | Dry 2024 | 30 | 2.1 | 48 percent | 7 percent. Upstream Rural | Wet 2025 | 30 | 3.4 | 52 percent | 13 percent. Town Centre | Dry 2024 | 32 | 6.8 | 71 percent | 38 percent. Town Centre | Wet 2025 | 32 | 9.2 | 68 percent | 56 percent. Downstream Estuary | Dry 2024 | 28 | 5.3 | 62 percent | 29 percent. Downstream Estuary | Wet 2025 | 28 | 7.9 | 65 percent | 46 percent. Method note: one laboratory, visual counting with partial chemical check, small seasonal samples.

writing.focus: Comparing evidence across groups and handling uncertainty
writing.prompt: This is original practice material, not an official test. The table below shows results from a university mentoring evaluation for first-year students in 2023 to 2024 at Northfield University. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words in about 20 minutes. Table data: Faculty | Mentored participants | Completed full programme | Reported improved study organisation | First-year continuation rate mentored | First-year continuation rate non-mentored. Arts | 120 | 78 percent | 64 percent | 88 percent | 81 percent. Science | 150 | 71 percent | 58 percent | 86 percent | 80 percent. Engineering | 95 | 66 percent | 61 percent | 84 percent | 79 percent. Evaluation note: participation was voluntary, survey response was 82 percent, and continuation is influenced by entry grades and other support.

writing.focus: Describing trends and contrasting qualified claims from data
writing.prompt: This is original practice material, not an official test. The table below shows average weekday public transport demand in the city of Merrivale in 2019 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words in about 20 minutes. Table data: Mode | Average weekday boardings 2019 | Average weekday boardings 2024 | Peak-hour share of daily boardings 2024 | Fare revenue as share of operating cost 2024. Bus | 182000 | 165000 | 34 percent | 42 percent. Tram | 96000 | 118000 | 41 percent | 55 percent. Suburban rail | 74000 | 71000 | 48 percent | 38 percent. Note: 2019 was pre-network change, 2024 includes a new tram extension opened in March 2023, figures exclude weekends and holidays.

writing.task: Task 2 · Local clean-ups and packaging rules
writing.focus: Evaluating qualified claims and comparing limited evidence
writing.prompt: This is original practice material, not an official test. Some people argue that local river clean-up projects do more to reduce freshwater plastic than national rules on packaging, while others argue that only national rules can address the causes. Discuss both views, compare the type of evidence each side might use, and give your own opinion with reasons. Acknowledge limitations in the evidence where relevant. Write at least 250 words in about 40 minutes.

writing.task: Task 2 · Compulsory university mentoring and transport priorities
writing.focus: Balanced argument with careful qualifications and trade-offs
writing.prompt: This is original practice material, not an official test. Some universities require all first-year students to join a mentoring programme, and some cities give priority to public transport investment over road expansion. Supporters say these policies improve long-term outcomes, while critics say they limit choice and ignore practical constraints. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of both approaches in terms of long-term benefits, individual choice, and practical constraints, and give your own opinion on which approach is more justified. Support your points with relevant examples and qualify general claims. Write at least 250 words in about 40 minutes.

speaking.task: Part 1 · Water, rivers and local environment
speaking.focus: Everyday experience with some qualified description
speaking.prompt: This is original practice. Answer in short, natural responses of 2 to 4 sentences, not memorised facts. Questions: How often do you walk near a river, lake or coast? What do you notice about litter or water quality in your area? Have you ever taken part in a clean-up or recycling activity? How has your use of single-use plastic changed in recent years? Why do you think some people are more concerned about water pollution than others?

This is original practice. Answer in short, natural responses. Questions: Did anyone help you when you started school, university or a new job? What kind of advice is most useful for new students? Do you prefer to learn alone or with guidance from others? How has the way students ask for help changed? Why might mentoring suit some students more than others?

speaking.task: Part 2 · Cue card: A mentoring or coaching experience
speaking.focus: Extended turn with organisation and reflection on limitations
speaking.prompt: This is original practice. Speak for 1 to 2 minutes. Describe a time when you received or gave mentoring, coaching or practical guidance. You should say: • who was involved and how you knew them • what the goal was and how long it lasted • what you or they actually did in the sessions • explain what was helpful and what was limited or uncertain about the support. You have about one minute to prepare and may make brief notes.

speaking.task: Part 2 · Cue card: A regular journey by public transport
speaking.focus: Extended description with comparison and detail
speaking.prompt: This is original practice. Speak for 1 to 2 minutes. Describe a journey you often make or once made by public transport such as bus, tram or train. You should say: • where you travelled from and to and why • which mode you used and when you travelled • what the service was like for comfort, time and cost • explain how satisfactory it was and what would improve it. You have about one minute to prepare and may make brief notes.

speaking.task: Part 3 · Evidence, environment and public choices
speaking.focus: Reasons and evaluation, not memorised facts
speaking.prompt: This is original practice. Discuss ideas with reasons and evaluation. Questions: Why should small sampling studies on rivers be treated with caution before making policy? How can decision makers compare evidence from a local study with evidence from national data? What are the advantages and limitations of voluntary mentoring compared with compulsory programmes? When should cities prioritise public transport over roads, and what trade-offs should be evaluated? How can the public be encouraged to interpret qualified claims carefully?
